title: fix(driver-sql): treat `id` as insert-only on the upsert merge path (#8622)
body:
Fixes #8622

A merge-path upsert on a business key silently rewrote the primary key of the row it merged into. `id` is now insert-only on that path, joining `created_at` and the `auto_number` columns.

## The defect, measured

The conflict target is a properly **backed** `unique: true` column, so this is the supported path — not an error path and not the unbacked-target family.

```
upsert({ email: 'x@b.com', title: 'first'  }, ['email'])
upsert({ email: 'x@b.com', title: 'second' }, ['email'])

[sqlite] before=[{id:'yMh3oywrp0Z6p-oJ', title:'first'}]
         after =[{id:'d8T8rUlTxlRlaUhN', title:'second'}]   idPreserved=false
[pg]     before=[{id:'T3AlYiyDi5buzGvW', title:'first'}]
         after =[{id:'TvbCTa5mydWPYP76', title:'second'}]   idPreserved=false
```

One row throughout, as intended — with a different primary key. `upsert` mints a nanoid for any call supplying none, and `id` rode the merge set, so `... do update set ..., "id" = excluded."id"` wrote the **losing** insert's fresh id over the winning row's. On the default `['id']` conflict target that clause is a no-op (both sides hold the same value), which is exactly why it stayed invisible.

`id` is what relationships, audit records, external id mappings and client-held references point at, so every one of them dangles afterwards, with no error on any dialect.

## Scope honesty on dialects

The card measured SQLite and live MySQL 8.0.46 and deliberately did not claim Postgres. **This PR raises Postgres and measures it**: system PG 16.13, `initdb` + `pg_ctl`, no container runtime, through the same knex + `pg` path. The rewrite reproduces there, so PG is no longer an inference.

MySQL is the one cell this container could not raise — no `mysqld`. See the pin note below.

## What changed

**1. `id` joins the insert-only set** (`insertOnlyUpsertColumns`). Resolved through `remoteColumn`, not as a literal: the shipped ADR-0015 §18 fixture in `sql-driver-external-columnmap.test.ts` binds a federated object with `columnMap: { ..., cust_id: 'id' }`, so `formatted` carries the key `cust_id` there and a literal `'id'` would filter nothing on exactly the objects federation exists to serve. Measured on the existing fixture, not defensive.

**2. The empty-merge-set fallback.** Excluding `id` made a branch reachable that could not fire before — with `id` always minted and always mergeable, the set could never empty. The bare `insertion.merge()` it falls to is merge-**ALL**: it re-admits every insert-only column. Measured on live PG mid-fix, an object whose only non-`id` column is an `auto_number`:

```
upsert({ email:'f@b.com' }, ['email'])   -> seeded, case_no=CASE-0005
upsert({ id: seededId },    ['id'])      -> rows=1, idPreserved=true
                                            case_no CASE-0005 -> CASE-0006   (#7011 defeated)
```

SQLite never reaches it — `stampInsertTimestamps` puts a mergeable `updated_at` in the payload on that dialect — so this is a one-cell blind spot that only raising PG could catch.

The fallback now uses the **conflict-target** columns present in the payload: on a conflict those matched by definition, so `excluded.target` is the stored value and the UPDATE is a provable no-op. It also reproduces the exact SQL `main` emits for this shape (`merge(['id'])`, `id` having been `main`'s only mergeable column there), so **this PR's net behavioural delta is the `id` exclusion and nothing else**.

The residual last-ditch `merge()` is left alone and filed as #8740 — it needs the conflict target absent from the payload, which means the INSERT never supplies it, so the target is NULL and cannot collide. The clean spelling is not accept-set-neutral (knex compiles `.ignore()` to MySQL's `insert ignore`, measured), so it wants a decision rather than a rider here.

## The accept set is unchanged

The same calls still succeed, still merge, and still advance `updated_at` and every other mergeable column. Each identity pin asserts the merge still happened (one row, `title` merged) **before** it asserts the id, so a green cannot be reached by refusing the call or by inserting a second row. Re-keying deliberately is still `update()`'s job, which writes exactly the columns it is handed — pinned on both cells.

## Reverse verification — direction predicted before running, and it is not uniform

**Leg 1, revert the `id` exclusion.** Predicted: the two identity pins red on both cells; `created_at` and `update()` green (independent limbs, not one lever); and the exhaustion pin **green**, because without the exclusion the merge set never empties. Measured, matched exactly: 4 failed, 20 passed.

**Leg 2, revert only the fallback.** Predicted: the exhaustion pin red on live PG, green on SQLite — the blind spot above. Measured, matched: 1 failed, 23 passed.

```
FAIL [#8622] every column insert-only (live postgres)
AssertionError: the merge-ALL fallback fired and renumbered the row - #7011's
exclusion is defeated whenever the insert-only set covers every column in the
payload: expected 'CASE-0006' to be 'CASE-0005'
```

The fix was committed before either leg, and restored with `git restore --source=HEAD`; byte-identity confirmed with `git hash-object` against `HEAD`'s blob.

## One pin flips from characterization to contract

#8592's `REPLACES the surviving row's primary key while merging on that wrong key` goes red under this fix by its own design — its failure message instructed whoever fixed it to rewrite it. It now asserts preservation, plus that the wrong-key merge itself still happens (so the pin cannot pass by the merge having simply stopped).

⚠️ **That one assertion is un-run here** — no `mysqld` in this container. It is carried on the driver-level argument that the merge set is built in-process before any dialect sees a statement, and the same claim is measured on SQLite and PG in the sweep above. CI's `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` job is the first runner to execute it.

The two pins around it are untouched: MySQL still merges on a key the caller never named, and still does not merge on the key it was given. Those belong to #8621, which is not addressed here.

## Verification

All at `2a4c120`, which is HEAD after the `main` merge and the final commit.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql test` — **99 files, 1868 passed, 32 skipped**, run with `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` attached and `TZ=America/New_York` so the matrix's three-way zone-skew guard is non-vacuous
- Gate union, all pass: `check:nul-bytes`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:type-source-resolution`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:type-check-debt` (on the built closure: 33 ledger entries re-measured, none above its recorded number), `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, `check:objectui-changeset`, `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-empty-changeset`

The changeset-family gates were not in the dispatched list; they came from re-deriving `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` against the actual diff, which includes the changeset this PR adds.

`main` was merged immediately before opening this PR — it brought in the sibling #8629 (`0f59584`), a different file in this package, no conflict.
